author: michelle
title: ITTF World Hopes Week in Sheffield: a big learning curve for England's Sai Prasanna Kumar and Isabella Xiao Xu
seo_title: ITTF World Hopes Week 2026 in Sheffield
description: ITTF World Hopes Week came to Sheffield, where England's Sai Prasanna Kumar and Isabella Xiao Xu trained and competed with the world's best under-12s.
standfirst: The ITTF's camp for the world's best under-12s came to the English Institute of Sport in Sheffield, ending in a competition where every game counted.
body: England's Sai Prasanna Kumar and Isabella Xiao Xu spent a week training and competing with some of the most promising under-12 players in the world when ITTF World Hopes Week came to Sheffield.

The camp, run by the sport's world governing body, was held at the English Institute of Sport in Sheffield. It combined a week of intensive training with a two-day Challenge competition at the end, and both English players held their own against opponents from around the world.
## A format where every game counts
The Challenge used an unusual format. Every match was played over four games, so results could finish 4-0, 3-1 or 2-2, and every game won counted towards a player's position on the leaderboard.

Charlotte Carey, Table Tennis England's national pathway coach, said the format was good for building resilience. "It's great that every set counts and there's still something to play for even if you are 3-0 down," she said.

She added that it could be harder to close out the fourth game when leading 3-0, and that players who drew 2-2 after trailing could feel they hadn't won even though they had taken two games for the leaderboard.

For Xu, the week was about how she handled matches as much as how she played them. "I really feel like I've improved in my way of how I play and how I react on the court, because everyone here is the top in their country," she said. She said the tough matches had taught her to stay calm and not become overconfident after a win, and added: "I'm very proud of myself, of being able to represent England."

Prasanna Kumar pointed to the coaching and the multiball training. "I learned how to have an aggressive backhand open up and my forehand's a lot stronger," he said. He said the players were better than he was used to at home and had taught him different styles.

Carey said meeting players and coaches from other countries and cultures was "invaluable experience" for both. Table Tennis England's video report described the week as a success for players, coaches and the ITTF.

World Hopes Week is part of the ITTF's development programme for leading under-12 players, bringing them together for training with international coaches before a competition. Hosting it meant two of England's youngest players could train in the same hall as the best of their age group from other countries.
It came in a big year for the sport in England, which hosted the ITTF World Team Championships in London earlier in 2026.

Both players return to England's junior programme, where the Cambridge Junior 4* is the next stop on the domestic calendar and offers a route to the National Championships. England's older juniors were in action at the weekend, when [Ella Pashley and Larry Trumpauskas retained their Under-21 National Cup titles](/news/pashley-trumpauskas-retain-u21-national-cup-2026.html).
